limits: Timeline events record outer dispatch identities before awaiting a result. They are not provider/backend calls, completed verifications, timed work, GPU evaluations or correctness counts.
ok=true means truthy return; false does not identify a particular runtime error or failure cause.
All events have attempt1, no nested timeline entries were projected, and exported counts match source-event counts for all eight rows.
Report rounds are report-authored with loop-counter fallback. rounds_committed is the direct warm_start counter. budget_used is direction cost.
Effective utilization, actual backend calls, GPU wait time, and causal reasons for performance differences remain unestablished.
Shared failure literals have no per-lineage attribution, can overlap, and are not additive failure-event counts.
Archive rows are not distinct program counts. Referenced kernel/patch files were not rehashed by this extraction; retained verifier fields are not fresh independent confirmations.
The final query enumerates published checkpoints and lineage finals, not every archive row; correctness, promotion, publication and final qualification are distinct.
Parent and donor IDs alone are not proof of source initialization or causal influence. Three separately listed ready initialization records establish recorded source loading at that scope.

source_semantics.budget_used: dispatched increments by direction cost before pipeline; deep_explore can cost more than one. Not a count of model/API calls.
source_semantics.rounds: report.rounds if report exists, otherwise loop round counter; not an independently reconstructed completed-round count.
source_semantics.rounds_committed: roundsCommitted is incremented on the improved branch after captureCanonicalSelection; returned directly as warm_start.rounds_committed.
source_semantics.source_scope: Inspected prepared H source reference; no additional installed-runtime closure verification in this audit.
source_semantics.timeline: tlAgent pushes an event before awaited agent dispatch; agent_guard sets ok=true for a truthy return. No timestamps/durations. A false event does not independently identify timeout, runtime failure, model failure or correctness.
